note: Mediterranean naval and territorial competition; Umayyad Iberia distinct from caliphal Damascus but participated in broader Mediterranean conflict.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Umayyad siege of Constantinople (717–718) and Byzantine iconoclasm (726) were causally linked: Emperor Leo III's religious reform was partly motivated by the need to rally theological unity against Islamic propaganda claiming that Christian image-worship was idolatrous; the Umayyad military pressure thus inadvertently triggered the Byzantine doctrinal crisis that fractured relations with Rome and created conditions for the Carolingian-papal alliance.
